rationale: Evidence: iteration 10 (kd 1.6) is the best design so far at 632.9. The oval finishes 20/20 at 1.81 s with max_error 0.013 and steering_oscillation 0.20, so it is not ringing. The s-bend finishes 18/20 with progress 0.98, and the slalom is still 0/20 with progress 0.16 and max_error 0.061. Body width is already at its maximum, so the 0.06 m off-track limit cannot move. Earlier single-variable kd steps (0.8 to 1.6) each raised s-bend completion with no measurable oval jitter. Changes to kp, base_speed, wheel_track, mass and sensor span all reduced oval reliability in earlier iterations, so I keep them fixed. This is the final iteration and the unseen track is scored once, so I keep the design close to the proven one and change one variable. Change: kd 1.6 to 1.8. Everything else is identical to iteration 10. Expected result: s-bend completion stays at 18 to 20 of 20 with progress near 0.98 to 1.0, the oval stays at 20/20 near 1.8 s, and the slalom progress changes little (it has plateaued near 0.14 to 0.16). Risk: higher kd amplifies sensor noise and may shift the unseen track's behaviour. If oval steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.3 or oval completion falls below 1.0, the fallback is kd 1.6. Hypotheses: (H1) derivative damping still limits alternating bends, so s-bend completion keeps improving with kd. (H2) The slalom is limited by entry speed or the 0.06 m off-track limit rather than damping, so it will not improve much from kd alone. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against 0.06, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and oval completion_time.
